name: Prince Buster
hook: A Kingston sound-system man and ska producer whose songs gave Madness its name and the Specials their first single.
blurb: Prince Buster was born Cecil Bustamente Campbell in Kingston in 1938, named after the labour leader Alexander Bustamante. He worked for Coxsone Dodd's sound system, then started his own, Voice of the People, which became a rival to Dodd's and Duke Reid's, and he recorded and produced ska records from the early 1960s. His songs 'Madness' (1963) and 'Al Capone' (1964) travelled to Britain with Jamaican migrants and the mod and skinhead crowds of the 1960s, and 'Al Capone' reached number 18 in Britain in February 1967. That is how they reached the 2 Tone generation. Twelve years later a London band named themselves Madness after one of his songs, and a Coventry band, the Specials, built their first single on 'Al Capone'. He died in 2016.
